question: Why does LiveKit Egress run as a separate process rather than recording directly within the agent?
options: Because Egress is cheaper to run as a standalone service
Because the agent does not have access to audio streams
Because running Egress separately ensures it does not affect call quality or agent performance
Because recording within the agent would require additional API keys
explanation: Egress runs as its own process that subscribes to the room independently. This separation ensures that the recording workload (capturing, encoding, uploading) does not consume resources needed for real-time call handling and AI agent processing.

question: In a two-party consent jurisdiction, what must your AI agent do before any substantive conversation begins?
options: Announce that the call is being recorded and obtain affirmative consent from the caller before proceeding
Record the call but delete it if the caller later objects
Silently start recording and disclose it at the end of the call
Send a text message to the caller informing them of the recording
explanation: Two-party consent jurisdictions require that all parties on a call are informed and give affirmative consent to being recorded. The AI agent must announce recording and obtain consent before any substantive conversation begins. The consent must be logged for compliance.
